material.body: Corrected evidence. The join button with an empty room name is a no-op (rooms.js joinNamedRoom rejects an empty name); the room button data-room=lobby sets the hash and reloads. After that the peer page (separate profile, port 9333) reaches #lobby, and the host page on the shared Chrome shows connecting with lobby 1/10 and no peer count. Both pages stay at peers 0 (local). Next witness: capture console and network events from both pages after the reload, to see whether the offer or announce is sent. Related: peer-offer-not-retried-join-race, peer-join-no-effect-separate-profile (superseded by this row).
material.resolution: Claim refuted on the live build; no code change.
material.subject: Two browser profiles stay connecting and never see each other
material.witness: Live Pages build 7f68d3bc (pages 40128978850 success). Isolated host (targetId 08D8F63253D90D149795C6B66FEC1164) and isolated peer (targetId 9BC6CD8426A9B1BB05625E2E59BC8D42), separate browser contexts. Host reads peers 3 (local) with peer-close; peer reads room lobby / peers 3 (net) (dispatch 1792893544786-6146-51979419161ecb5b). Both pages are joined to peers; neither stays connecting. Claim refuted. Earlier 42 frames in 20s (dispatch 1792893081258-5746-699eb0e352024f06).
